status: experimental; validated release-based implementation, not current upstream main

environment.model_variant_note: User-provided uncensored NVFP4 conversion; results are not a qualification of all artifacts

method.prompt: Explain how a mixture-of-experts transformer routes tokens, why an expert cache helps, and how PCIe transfers affect response speed. Use complete sentences.
method.ttft: perf_counter from before HTTP dispatch to first nonempty streamed content delta
method.memory: Windows GPUProcessMemory DedicatedUsage summed for the server process, divided by 2**20
method.system_gpu_mib: nvidia-smi used,free; system-wide, not process dedicated accounting
method.acceptance: real sleep event followed by wake; exact output equality; 96 output tokens; nonzero dedicated-memory counter
limitations: Sequential workstation campaigns, not randomized; changing background load
Baseline and preliminary campaigns predate final safety/calibration changes
Client TTFT includes admission wake, which may be recorded as native queue time
No causal decode-throughput improvement is established

reference_output:
In a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) transformer, token routing is managed by a lightweight gating network that dynamically selects a small subset of specialized expert networks for each input token. Instead of activating all parameters in the model, this router calculates affinity scores and directs the token to only the top-k most relevant experts, allowing the model to scale its capacity significantly while keeping computational costs per token relatively low.

An expert cache helps improve efficiency by storing frequently accessed or recently used expert
